chapter_title_en: Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ზღვა გაიარა ავთანდილ, მივა ტანითა მჭევრითა.
ნახეს ქალაქი, მოცული გარე ბაღისა ტევრითა,
გვარად უცხონი ყვავილნი, ფერითა მეტად ბევრითა,
და მის ქვეყანისა სიტურფე რა გაგაგონო მევ, რითა!
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil crossed the sea; with stately form went he. They saw a city engirt by a thicket of garden, with wondrous kinds of flowers of many and many a hue. In what way canst thou understand the loveliness of that land!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1061; Wardrop Stanza 1039): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: With three ropes they moored the ship to the shore of those gardens. Avt’handil clad his form in a cloak and sat on a bench. They brought out men that were porters, provided with drachmas. That knight bargains, acts as chief (of the caravan), and thereby conceals himself.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1062; Wardrop Stanza 1040): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მოვიდა მისი მებაღე, ბაღსა ეახლნეს რომელსა.
მას ყმასა უჭვრეტს შეფრფინვით პირსა, ელვათა მკრთომელსა,
ავთანდილ უხმო, ეუბნა კაცსა არ სიტყვა მცთომელსა:
და “ვისნი ხართ, ვინ ხართ, რა ჰქვიან მეფესა აქა მჯდომელსა?
stanzas.english_translation: Thither came the gardener of him at whose garden they had landed; with ecstasy he gazes at the knight's face flashing like lightning. Avt’handil hailed him, he spoke to the man with faultless words: "Whose men are ye, who are ye? how call they the king reigning here?
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1063; Wardrop Stanza 1041): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“წვრილად მითხარ ყველაკაი”, ყმა მას კაცსა ეუბნების,
“რა ლარია უფრო ძვირად, ან იეფად რა იხსნების?”
ჰკადრა: “ვხედავ პირსა თქვენსა, მზისა პირად მემეცნების;
და რაცა ვიცი, მართლად გკადრებ, მრუდი არა არ გემცნების.
stanzas.english_translation: "Tell me all in detail," quoth the knight to that man; "what stuff is dearer, or what is bought up cheap?" He said: "I see, thy face seems to me like the face of the sun. Whatever I know I will tell thee truly; I will by no means inform thee crookedly.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1064; Wardrop Stanza 1042): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: "The Sea Realm is this, ten months’ (travel) in extent, this is the city of Gulansharo 1, full of much loveliness. Hither everything fair cometh by ships sailing from sea to sea. Melik Surkhavi rules, perfect in good fortune and wealth.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1065; Wardrop Stanza 1043): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აქა მოსლვითა გაყმდების, კაციმცა იყო ბერები:
სმა, გახარება, თამაში, ნიადაგ არს სიმღერები,
ზამთარ და ზაფხულ სწორად გვაქვს ყვავილი ფერად-ფერები.
და ვინცა გვიცნობენ, გვნატრიან, იგიცა, ვინა მტერები.
stanzas.english_translation: "Even if he be old, a man is rejuvenated by coming hither; drinking, rejoicing, tilting and songs are unceasing; summer and winter alike we have many-hued flowers; whoever knoweth us envieth us, even they who are our foes.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1066; Wardrop Stanza 1044): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: "Great merchants can find nought more profitable than this: They buy, they sell, they gain, they lose; a poor man will be enriched in a month; from all quarters they gather merchandise; the penniless by the end of the year have money laid by.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1067; Wardrop Stanza 1045): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: "I am gardener to Usen, chief of the merchants. I shall tell thee somewhat of the manner of his ordinance: [paragraph continues] This is his garden, your resting-place for the day; first it is necessary to show him all the fairest of your goods.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1068; Wardrop Stanza 1046): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რა შემოვლენ დიდ-ვაჭარნი, მას ნახვენ და ძღვენსა სძღვნიან,
უჩვენებენ, რაცა ჰქონდეს სხვაგან ლარსა ვერ გახსნიან,
უტურფესსა სეფედ დასხმენ, ფასსა მუნვე დაუთვლიან;
და მათ მაშინვე ააზატებს, ვითა სწადდეს, დაჰყიდიან.
stanzas.english_translation: "When great merchants arrive they see him and give him gifts, they show him what they have, elsewhere they cannot unpack their goods; for the king they set aside the best, they straightway count out the price; thereupon he frees them to sell as they please.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1069; Wardrop Stanza 1047): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: "His duty it is to receive such honourable folk as you, he orders the caterers how to entertain them fitly; he is not now here, what avails it me to speak of him To meet you and carry you away with him, pressing you politely, is the way he should treat you.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1070; Wardrop Stanza 1048): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: "P’hatman Khat’hun, the lady, his wife, is at home, a hospitable hostess, amiable, not rough. I shall inform her of your arrival, she will take you in as one of her own folk, she will send a man to meet you, you shall enter the city by daylight."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1071; Wardrop Stanza 1049): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ავთანდილ უთხრა: “წადიო, აგრე ქმენ, რაცა გწადიან”.
მებაღე მირბის, იხარებს, ოფლი მკერდამდის ჩასდიან.
ხათუნსა უთხრა ამბავი: “მე ესე დამიქადიან,
და ყმა მოვა, მისთა მჭვრეტელთა შუქნი მზედ გაიცადიან.
stanzas.english_translation: Avt’handil said: "Go, do whatever thou desirest." The gardener runs, he rejoices, sweat pours down to his breast. He tells his tidings to the lady: "I boast of this: a youth comes, to them that look on him his rays seem like the sun.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1072; Wardrop Stanza 1050): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ვაჭარი ვინმე პატრონი არს ქარავნისა დიდისა,
საროსა მსგავსი ნაზარდი და მთვარე დღისა შვიდისა;
ჰშვენის ჯუბა და მოხვევა ძოწეულისა რიდისა.
და მიმიხმო, მკითხა ამბავი და ნირი ლართა სყიდისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "He is some merchant, chief of a great caravan, well-grown like a cypress, a moon of seven days, his coat and the fold of his coral-hued turban become him; he called me, asked me tidings and the tariff for the purchase of goods."
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1073; Wardrop Stanza 1051): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: Dame P’hatman rejoiced; she sent ten slaves to meet him; they prepared the caravanserais, she stored their wares. The rose-cheeked, crystal and ruby, glass, jet, entered; they who looked on him compared his feet to the panther's, his palms to the lion's (paws).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1074; Wardrop Stanza 1052): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: There was a hubbub, the hosts of the town all assembled; they pressed on this side and on that, saying: "We will gaze on him till sleeptime." Some were carried away by desire, some had their souls reft from them; their wives grew weary of them, their husbands were left contemned.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1075; Wardrop Stanza 1053): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: P’hatman, Usen's wife, met him in front of the door, joyful she saluted him, she showed her pleasure; they greeted each other, they went in and seated themselves. As I have observed, his coming annoyed not Dame P’hatman.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1076; Wardrop Stanza 1054): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
ფატმან ხათუნ თვალად მარჯვე, არ ყმაწვილი, მაგრა მზმელი,
ნაკვთად კარგი, შავ-გრემანი, პირ-მსუქანი, არ-პირხმელი,
მუტრიბთა და მომღერალთა მოყვარული, ღვინის-მსმელი,
და დია ედვა სასალუქო დასაბურავ-ჩასაცმელი.
stanzas.english_translation: Dame P’hatman was attractive to the eye, not young but brisk, of a good figure, dark in complexion, plump-faced, not wizened, a lover of (female) minstrels and singers, a wine-drinker; she had abundance of elegant gowns and head-dresses.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1077; Wardrop Stanza 1055): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
მას ღამესა ფატმან ხათუნ უმასპინძლა მეტად კარგა.
ყმამან უძღვნა ძღვენი ტურფა, მიმღებელთა თქვეს თუ: “ვარგა”.
ფატმანს მისი მასპინძლობა უღირს, ღმერთო, არ დაკარგა;
და სვეს და ჭამეს, დასაწოლად ყმა გავიდა ღამით გარ გა.
stanzas.english_translation: That night Dame P’hatman entertained him right well. The knight presented beautiful gifts; they that received them said: "They are worthy!" P’hatman's entertainment of him was worth while; by God! she lost not. When they had drunken and eaten, the knight went outs to sleep.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1078; Wardrop Stanza 1056): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
დილასა ლარი ყველაი უჩვენა, გაახსნევინა,
ტურფანი სეფედ გარდასხნა, ფასიცა დაათვლევინა,
ვაჭართა უთხრა: “წაიღეთ”, აჰკიდა, გააწევინა;
და “თქვენ ვითა გინდა, ვაჭრობდით, ნუ გამამჟღავნებთ, მე ვინა”.
stanzas.english_translation: In the morning he showed all his wares, he had them all unpacked; the fairest were laid aside for the king, he had the price counted out; he said to the merchants: "Take them away!" He loaded them, (and) had them carried away. He said: "Sell as ye will; reveal not who I am!"
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1079; Wardrop Stanza 1057): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

stanzas.english_translation: The knight was clad as a merchant; he was by no means dressed in his proper raiment. Sometimes P’hatman calls on him, sometimes he visits P’hatman. They sat together; they conversed with refined discourse. Absence from him was death to P’hatman, as Ramin's was to Vis. 1
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 43 ('Story of Avtandil's Arrival in Gulansharo', Stanza 1080; Wardrop Stanza 1058): Part of the narrative sequence in which avtandil sails into Gulansharo ('City of Roses'), the bustling Renaissance-like maritime trading metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, meets the head gardener, and is welcomed by Patman Khatun, the vivacious wife of chief merchant Usen.

act_title: Act IV: Gulansharo, Patman Khatun & Tidings of Kadjeti

location.desc: Mercantile port metropolis of the Kingdom of the Seas, home of Usen and Patman Khatun.

key_maxim_ka: მომცნა ფრთენი და აღვფრინდე, მივჰხვდე მას ჩემსა ნდომასა
key_maxim_en: Grant me wings that I may fly, reach my desire! (Stanza 1304)
